_comment: NOT ON THE RELEASE PATH. The release certificate is taken from the ETHUSD profile, which #332 names primary and which the checklist runs by name; this one has no launch entry and is invoked by hand. It exists because venue behaviour is per PAIR rather than per adapter - lot minimum, tick size, decimals, liquidity - so a certificate over ETHUSD certifies ETHUSD. What differs from the primary: the symbol, the sizes (lot_size 0.0001 BTC; Kraken's BTCUSD minimum is 0.00006 since October 2026), the re-arm cap (max_rearm_attempts 6 here, 0 = unbounded there), and the protective-level phase, which only the primary runs. CAUTION: `field_study_certificate_cli.py generate --latest` takes the newest certificate run by its start, whichever profile ran it - so a BTCUSD run started after an ETHUSD one becomes the certified run unless `--profile kraken_spot_ethusd_field_study` names the primary. The certificate records `profile` and `symbol` and prints both at generation. REAL MONEY: adapter_type live, dry_run false.

deployment._comment: Do this profile's sessions form ONE deployment whose ledger rows join into one history? MANDATORY — there is no safe default. Declare true only on a profile you are actually deploying; the CLI can narrow it (--one-off) but never widen it.

decision_logic_config._comment: max_session_cost_usd re-chosen 2026-09-08 from the first correctly-measured run, not inherited. A full 20-phase run books $0.182 today and will book ~$0.354 once #337 corrects the fee rates — the venue charged exactly $0.35424 and the account moved $0.3584. At the old 0.5 that is 71 % of the ceiling after #337, so one re-armed limit phase would self-abort a release gate with no defect present. At 1.00 a normal run sits at 35 % and the brake still trips at 2.8x a normal run, which is what it is for. The ceiling is checked against OUR booking, so it moves with #337; the account-side figure lives in the certificate as `account_delta`.

phase_sequence._comment: The live STOP path (#500). A buy stop rests ABOVE the market and is accepted, confirmed resting, then cancelled at the venue — no fill, therefore no fee. What it proves cannot be proven by a mock: the trigger mapping on the wire (Kraken's `price` carries the trigger, not a limit), the submit-response route that confirms the broker reference, the poll loop reading the stop world, and the cancel path finding the order there rather than among the limits. Both numbers differ from the limit phases ON PURPOSE. A buy stop's order value is lots x TRIGGER, and on ETHUSD a stop worth about $5.00 was refused for its cost (measured 2026-09-07: EOrder:Cost minimum not met), so this one keeps a margin: 0.00015 BTC is about $13 at October 2026 prices. The size used to be the ETH profile's 0.004, copied over — at BTC prices a buy stop of that size holds several hundred USD. And unlike a limit phase this order must NOT fill: a fill here means the trigger was mis-sided, so the offset is wide enough that a 30-second window cannot reach it.

Its own size ON PURPOSE (2026-10-18). The phase sells half, and the half and the rest each have to clear the venue's minimum size: at lot_size 0.0001 the half is 0.00005, below Kraken's BTCUSD minimum since October 2026 (0.00006), and the executor refuses such a partial close before anything is sent (REMAINDER_BELOW_MINIMUM). 0.00015 leaves 0.000075 on each side.
